title: Uniform noise stability from a sensitivity bound
statement: Let $B=(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a family of sets of real-valued functions on Boolean cubes, and suppose every function in every $B_n$ takes values in $\{-1,1\}$. Let $\varepsilon:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be nonnegative for $0\le\delta\le1/2$, with $\varepsilon(\delta)\to0$ as $\delta\to0^+$, and suppose that $\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)\le\varepsilon(\delta)$ for every $n$, every $f\in B_n$, and every $0<\delta\le1/2$. Then there exists a function $\eta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ taking values in $[0,1]$ on $[0,1/2]$, tending to zero as $\delta\to0^+$, such that $\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)\le\eta(\delta)$ for all such $n,f$ and $0<\delta\le1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: The sensitivity bound holds for every dimension, member, and $0<\delta\le1/2$
replaced:
Let $B=(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a family of sets of functions $\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\}$ and let $\varepsilon:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $\varepsilon(\delta)\geq0$ for $0\leq\delta\leq1/2$, $\lim_{\delta\to0^{+}}\varepsilon(\delta)=0$ and $\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)\leq\varepsilon(\delta)$ for every $n$, $f\in B_n$ and $0<\delta\leq1/2$.
Then $B$ is uniformly noise-stable: there exists $\eta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with $0\leq\eta(\delta)\leq1$ on $[0,1/2]$, $\lim_{\delta\to0^{+}}\eta(\delta)=0$ and $\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)\leq\eta(\delta)$ for every such $n,f,\delta$, where $\operatorname{NS}_{\delta}(f)=\Pr[f(X)\neq f(Y)]$, $X$ is uniform on the cube and $Y$ flips each coordinate independently with probability $\delta$.
